verbatim_excerpt:
23-21 Floor Area Regulations for R1 Through R5 Districts

In the districts indicated, the maximum #residential# #floor area ratio# shall be as set forth in the following table. Separate maximum #residential# #floor area ratios# are set forth for standard #zoning lots# and #zoning lots# that are #qualifying residential sites#.

MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA RATIO FOR R1-R5 DISTRICTS

[table - see structured `table` field]

1 For standard #zoning lots# with a #lot area# of 4,000 square feet or more, the maximum #residential# #floor area# associated with any single #dwelling unit# shall not exceed an equivalent #floor area ratio# of 0.60.

table.caption: MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA RATIO FOR R1-R5 DISTRICTS

footnotes.1: For standard #zoning lots# with a #lot area# of 4,000 square feet or more, the maximum #residential# #floor area# associated with any single #dwelling unit# shall not exceed an equivalent #floor area ratio# of 0.60.

notes: RECAPTURED 2026-09-11 FROM RAW HTML. The prior capture (retrieved 2026-07-21 for the M4-T001 R5 pilot) was PARTIAL: it carried only 4 rows, all R5 variants, under a section title reading 'R1 Through R5 Districts'. R1, R2, R2X, R3, R4 and every letter variant were absent. This capture carries all 5 printed rows covering all 18 districts.

DEFECT FOUND BY THIS RECAPTURE - footnote 1 scope was misattributed. Verified at the byte level: the source markup is 0.75<sup>1</sup>, i.e. footnote 1 is attached to the STANDARD value of the FIRST ROW ONLY (R1-2A, R1-1, R1-2, R2A, R2, R3A, R3X, R3-1, R3-2). No other row carries any superscript. The 0.60 single-dwelling-unit equivalent-FAR cap therefore does NOT apply to R2X, R4, R4A, R4B, R4-1, R5, R5A, R5B or R5D.

CONSEQUENCE for existing draft work: the prior snapshot rendered footnote 1 as a standalone body paragraph rather than a row-scoped footnote, and services/api/app/rules/rulesets/r5_residential_far.rule.json consequently carries exception 'single_dwelling_unit_equivalent_far_cap' (effect documented_limitation, citation_ref zr-23-21) on the R5 family, where the source does not impose it. The rule is status needs_review and the exception is a SURFACED LIMITATION, not a computed value, so no number is wrong - but it over-warns on every R5 result with a caveat the law does not attach there. To be corrected when the R1-R12 FAR family is authored. M4-T001 is awaiting_gate, not accepted, so this is draft engineering and no accepted artifact is affected.
'Qualifying residential sites' is a conditional/eligibility program (higher FAR). Whether a given lot qualifies is a separate legal determination and is NOT decided by this snapshot or by any agent.
Unlike ZR 23-22, NO row in this table is conditioned on #wide street# proximity, and no district appears twice. Every R1-R5 district is a flat lookup once footnote 1's scope is respected.

CROSS-CHECK: the owner supplied an independent PDF of this section generated by https://zr.planning.nyc.gov on 2026-09-10. All 5 rows, all values, the footnote and the 12/5/2024 amendment date match this HTML capture exactly.
Nothing in this record is a Verified zoning determination. Verified requires an M4 published rule with G6 qualified-human legal approval.
